gaps: P0–P1: nothing usable; P6: every modern candidate shows a different place named Brest
notes: #3 is Brześć Kujawski (Poland); #20–#23 are Brest in North Macedonia and Brest pri Igu in Slovenia. #1 (Merian, dated ‘1630–40’) is the same view as #2 and is described as engraved by Peeters, so its date is doubtful. #4/#5 (Antoine Aveline, ‘about 1700’) skipped: Aveline was born in 1691, so the date is doubtful. #7 is dated only 1820–55 by the archive (it shows a paddle steamer and no bridge over the Penfeld, so probably the 1840s–50s); #8 (Skelton, 1838, view from the roadstead) is a firmly dated but weaker alternative for P3. #13 (the château from the swing bridge) is an alternative P4 photochrom.
